judged_text: Literal "refresh_token" string injected into stored credentials: when the response lacks refresh_token (the documented sync response is only access_token + expiry), the code sets data.refresh_token = "refresh_token" — the literal string — and Office365 then spreads tokenResponse.data over existing credentials and persists it (Zoom likewise), clobbering the real refresh token; if credential sync is later disabled or the endpoint removed, those credentials are permanently broken (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26)

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly mutates successful parses to inject a literal `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the response lacks one (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26). In Office365, the returned object is then spread over existing credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), which will overwrite the real stored refresh token with this literal string and then persist it via `prisma.credential.update` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). This is a concrete credential-corrupting behavior introduced by the diff and matches the finding’s concern about breaking future refreshes if sync mode is disabled later.
